I was stationed in Spain for years.

Madrid and Barcelona are the two common spots to see, buy if You like history, Toledo is just outside Madrid. It is the old capital and a city inside a fortress. Very cool to see. New Toledo, the town just outside, has modern food and hotels.

Just making a small effort at speaking Spanish ("Hola, buena") will often get any English speakers to be more than happy to speak English for you. Often, they speak British so be prepared for some weird words and phrases. Bathroom is marked "baño", but also referred to as loo (lew) or W.C./watercloset.

Watch out for gypsies and Africans. No, this isn't racism, it is no joke. Every corner in big cities you will have people trying to scam you. You will be offered flowers, trinkets, whatever "for free"; never take anything, don't even look at the trinket or the person offering it. You will just be asking for trouble.

When on foot, stay on main roads unless you want to experience a mugging first-hand. People can easily spot tourists, and Spanish people are massively under and unemployed.

Look up where you are going to visit. Plazas are a common place to visit and often have a lot of sites around them to visit, too. However, some plazas are famous for prostitutes... so... if you got kids or that bothers you, avoid those areas. Prostitution is completely legal, so expect to see them in a lot of places. Just shake your head no (or don't make eye contact) and keep walking.

It is now May, so the rainy season should be ending and temperature bearable. July and August is like living in an oven. Winds from the south will bring a fine sand in summer that sticks to everything. Hopefully your trip is soon.

Speaking of summer, they do not use air conditioning in the way we do. Mostly they just open windows and let the breeze in. Make sure the hotel you stay in offers air conditioning (air con). You can thank me after the trip.

Small convenience thing, if you need wifi, they pronounce it "wee-fee". They have no clue what you are talking about if you say it wifi.

And if you do speak Mexican Spanish, realize they speak Castillan in the north and Andalusian in the south, which are different dialects. There are a few differences.

That's all I can think of right now. Hope you have a good trip.
